audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields (late, whys[6], spikes[1], wants.you[2]) state that 'Null Sphere interrupts his Demonic Ascension channel' and build a win condition on it. Riot's Demonic Ascension text describes a transformation, not a channel: 'Swain transforms into a demon and drains health from nearby enemy champions, minions, and neutral monsters... This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions.' A form that persists indefinitely is not something an interrupt cancels, and swain.json carries no channel flag on R — unlike Quinn's Behind Enemy Lines, Shen's Stand United and Poppy's Keeper's Verdict, which all do carry it in the same kit library.
audit.why: This is the load-bearing claim of the matchup's late game, so if it is wrong the whole plan is wrong. I removed it rather than leave it shipped; removing a possibly-true fact is recoverable, shipping a false one is not.
audit.corrected: The interrupt claim is gone from all four fields, replaced with what the kits do support: buy Grievous Wounds against the drain, and burst him before it ramps.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove's actual timing is never stated, and Ravenous Flock is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Riot's Nevermove text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The root is on the RETURN leg, not the outbound — which means the wave passing through you is not the moment to panic, and you have the whole return travel to step off its path. The page said only 'blink the instant his E root projectile is in the air', which points at the wrong leg. Riot's Ravenous Flock text: 'Swain's ravens collect Soul Fragments that heal him and permanently increase his maximum health', and Vision of Empire grants him a fragment for every champion it hits — so eating his poke literally makes him permanently bigger.
audit.corrected: The return-leg root is now in mid, whys[4], spikes[1], winCon, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5] and loading. Ravenous Flock and the Soul Fragment loop are in early, whys[3], whys[5], late, wants.foe[2] and enemyWin, with Morellonomicon named in wants.you[2] and breakdown.cooldowns.

notes: Judgement call flagged for the user: the page asserted in four places that Null Sphere interrupts Demonic Ascension. Riot's description of that ultimate is a transformation that 'is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions', and swain.json carries no channel flag on R while Quinn's, Shen's and Poppy's ultimates all do in the same library. I removed the claim rather than leave a load-bearing interaction on a live page that the source data does not support — but I did not have a way to prove it in-client, so this one is worth a second pair of eyes. The genuine Null Sphere interrupt in my slice is Shen's Stand United, which is flagged as a channel. Also worth knowing: _missing-interactions.json contains 'Swain can cancel your Null Sphere (Q) with Nevermove (E)' for the mid-lane copy, built on the same bad channel flag on Null Sphere; not written.
